HRA Analysis: LOCHINVAR SON (5) showed good gate speed two starts ago to lead before handing over and was running on nicely into second not beaten far by Dingane. He appears to find a suitable race where he is reasonably well handicapped and should go close to winning. ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (6) made a break early last time out and was taken out of play there as a result. He was a good winner three starts ago at this track and a similar effort would see him go close in this race. MY NAMES BRUCE (3) wasn’t beaten too far in fourth two starts ago when beaten by Dingane. He then made a break last time out and took no part. He can look to bounce back. LIZZIES SON (7) has done plenty wrong in recent race starts which has seen him completing plenty of trials. He is capable of figuring in a race of this nature if he brings his manners. SELECTIONS: LOCHINVAR SON (5), ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (6), MY NAMES BRUCE (3), LIZZIES SON (7) SUGGESTED BET: LOCHINVAR SON (5) to win.

MAJOR SLIP UP (8) sat without cover last time out at Marburg and was able to run a very good second there behind The Casual Goose. He looks likely to get a lot more favours in the run this time drawn inside the back row and should be hard to hold out late. NO FAMILY LIKEMINE (1) should have the gate speed to drive through and lead in the early stages of this race. He led two starts ago and was run down late by Magicol Ideal who has been in good form recently. He should be hard to run down. COPY WRITER (3) sat without cover last time out at Redcliffe and was well beaten there. She has since been freshened up and may be an improver in this race from a good draw. THREE CHORD RIFF (2) was shuffled back early last time out at Redcliffe and finished it off fairly into fifth. She should get a good run in this race from an ideal draw. SELECTIONS: MAJOR SLIP UP (8), NO FAMILY LIKEMINE (1), COPY WRITER (3), THREE CHORD RIFF (2) SUGGESTED BET: MAJOR SLIP UP (8) to win.

RACANA (9) has been racing in very good form and appears to be closing in on another win. She sat without cover last time out and was a very good second behind Bling The Noise in good time for the grade at Redcliffe. She looks hardest to beat. BURNS BAY (10) got back from a wide draw two starts ago and was finishing that race off stylishly into second behind October Racketeer. He looks set to secure a good run off the speed again in this race and should be running on again. ITS BACK PAGE NEWS (7) broke through for a well deserved win last time out when zipping across to lead before holding off Aqua Cruiser late who had the run on her back. She draws widest this time and may be shuffled back or forced to do some work. TAKE A CHANCE (5) secured a great run on speed with cover last time out and loomed up as a winning chance but just wasn’t quite able to run down Luvn Osman who has since run well again. SELECTIONS: RACANA (9), BURNS BAY (10), ITS BACK PAGE NEWS (7), TAKE A CHANCE (5) SUGGESTED BET: RACANA (9) to win.

CAPTAIN JAZZ (7) was an incredibly impressive winner last time out. She made a break at the start and lost plenty of ground before catching them up and sprinting over the top late to score a really good win. She draws widest this time but is a filly which looks destined to win better races. CRIPPA MAX (5) was forced to sit without cover last time out and wasn’t beaten far finishing fourth. He has previously sat without cover and beaten one of his rivals in this race BETTOR BE BOHDI (1). He should get a similar run in this race and can be thereabouts again. INTERPRETATION (8) was a good winner at this track last time out over the 2138 when securing the leaders back trail and was able to beat former kiwi Barracuda. She should get a good run again in this race following a gate speed horse. BETTOR BE BOHDI (1) has good early speed and should lead in the early stages. He was shuffled a long way back last time out in a race taken out by INTERPRETATION (8). He looks likely to get a lot more favours in the run this time. SELECTIONS: CAPTAIN JAZZ (7), CRIPPA MAX (5), INTERPRETATION (8), BETTOR BE BOHDI (1) SUGGESTED BET: INTERPRETATION (8) each way.

LOCHINVAR JEWELLS (2) has very good gate speed and should be able to work to the lead in this race. Was able to show good gate speed two starts ago to lead before kicking clear and really stopped late to be run down by Theresachance and Quik Change. She had set a strong tempo in that race but she does step up to the longer journey in this race which could be a query. TREACHEROUS BELLE (5) has no gate speed at all which often sees her shuffled back in races which was the case last time out when being shuffled back on the pegs. She finished the race off fairly into fifth when eventually clear. HEZA MAYWYN (1) has the perfect draw in this race to follow one of the likely favoured runners in the race. He was shuffled back last time out and was running on late into fourth behind Shez A Punter. UBETONRED (9) secured a good run up on speed last time out and was running on well in a quick last half for Redcliffe when finishing fourth. That effort backed up a good effort two starts ago when running second to his stablemate Art Jester. SELECTIONS: LOCHINVAR JEWELLS (2), TREACHEROUS BELLE (5), HEZA MAYWYN (1),UBETONRED (9) SUGGESTED BET: LOCHINVAR JEWELLS (2) to win.

GEM PUNTER PETE (3) draws the best of the main chances in this race and may be able to work his way to the lead early. He was shuffled back early last time out before appearing to run through the line nicely late. He is likely to have derived benefit from the run and should go well in this race. MISTER MANAGER (8) sat without cover two starts ago and battled on well there for a close second behind Race For Riches. He couldn’t quite back that up last start when sitting without cover and fading late behind Spirit Of Anarchy. He can bounce back with luck in running. FLYING COLOURS (10) secured a good run on the pegs last time out and finished the race off fairly into fifth behind Spirit Of Anarchy. He should get a good run off the speed and can be running on late. DRAGON (7) secured a good run last time out and was running on late into third behind Spirit Of Anarchy. He may get less favours in the run this time from the wide draw but can be running on late again. SELECTIONS: GEM PUNTER PETE (3), MISTER MANAGER (8), FLYING COLOURS (10), DRAGON (7) SUGGESTED BET: GEM PUNTER PETE (3) to win.

MIKI B (2) looks the leader early in this race from a good draw. He led and copped pressure last time out over the 2138 and was run down late by Braventreacherous who is in brilliant form at the moment. He should be hard to run down. WILLIAMS (1) should get a good run potentially behind the leader in this race. He was forced to sit without cover last time out and battled away gamely there when not beaten far by Betterthanfederer who had a good run off the speed. SWEET AGENDA (8) should get a good run through early on the back of Williams in this race. She was shuffled back last time out at Redcliffe in a race taken out by Beyond Doubt where she was working through the line well late. DREAMALITTLEDREAM (9) secured a good run close to the speed last time out in a genuinely run race and just wasn’t quite able to show her excellent turn of foot at the end of the race. She steps back to the 1660 in this race which could be suitable. SELECTIONS: MIKI B (2), WILLIAMS (1), SWEET AGENDA (8), DREAMALITTLEDREAM (9) SUGGESTED BET: MIKI B (2) to win.

SALLY BIGTIME (2) last time she led she was able to run fast time over the 1660 beating quality Dixon runners Ruby Rules and Fate Awaits. She impressed through the carnival running a number of good races against the top mares. She has excellent gate speed and should lead for a long way in this race. FERNCO NEL (10) zipped across early before taking a sit on Heza Punk Rocker last time out and was able to run a good second to that horse. He draws the back row this time but is a horse that is generally best when sat up and saved for one run which could see him suited. TREMENDOUS SENSATION (3) was very unlucky last time out when shuffled a long way back before getting clear and hitting the line powerfully behind Golden Fire. She draws favourably on the front row in this race and should settle close enough. AIR EXPRESS (5) sat without cover last time out at this track and was able to score a dominant win there. He steps right up in grade into this race but has always been a horse with an abundance of ability and has seemingly gotten better with age in terms of his tractability. SELECTIONS: SALLY BIGTIME (2), FERNCO NEL (10), TREMENDOUS SENSATION (3), AIR EXPRESS (5) SUGGESTED BET: SALLY BIGTIME (2) to win.

DOUGS FLAME (9) has raced without luck for a considerable period of time. She was eye catching last time out when getting back in the run before flashing home late into fourth in a race taken out by Braventreacherous. She should be running on again. BETTORS MOON (3) was left without cover last time out and ran a very good third in fast time. She looks to find a race where she should be able to find a prominent position again and can be fighting out the finish. QUEEN LILIBET (10) was a good winner last time out when suited racing off the speed in a genuinely run race. She is likely to be suited again in another race which looks as though is should be genuinely run. FAR OUT RINGO (1) lands in this race first up for the stable of Jack Butler. He has moderate early speed which could see him drive through early before having options from there. SELECTIONS: DOUGS FLAME (9), BETTORS MOON (3), QUEEN LILIBET (10), FAR OUT RINGO (1) SUGGESTED BET: DOUGS FLAME (9) to win. A No More Than Two Wins event kicks off tonight, where IDEN ELIZA JANE (1) will be looking to break through at start 17. She draws the pole and will be attempting to hold the front after a handy effort last start when sitting outside the leader. SOHO TIGER LILY (7) drops back in grade after competing in the Oaks last week and possesses terrific gate speed, so expect her to be driven aggressively from the outside gate in an attempt to find the pegs, where she may take plenty of running down over the mile. REMMINGTON (4) is a lightly raced six-year-old who won nicely at her first start in the state two starts back, and expect him to again push forward from the middle of the front row to give herself every chance. B K WINDERMERE (2) is the other front-row runner and resumes from a lengthy spell, but trialled nicely enough recently to suggest she can be competitive here. With good early speed expected, the back-row runners should also get their chance, including I GOTTA GO (9), who has been consistent throughout his career and battled on well after copping pressure throughout last start against older horses. MIRA DOMINA (10) narrowly went down when leading in fast time over the short trip last start and clearly appreciates the mile distance. Selections:SOHO TIGER LILY (7), I GOTTA GO (9), MIRA DOMINA (10), IDEN ELIZA JANE (1)

SWEET DIXIE (2) should have enough gate speed to find the pegs, which could make her difficult to run down. She was good first up from a break two weeks ago and gets into this race well with the mares claim. EYE SEE AMOUR (5) gets back to a front-row draw after his manners have let him down on a few occasions of late. However, if he puts his best foot forward and gets away cleanly, his class should take him a long way in this field. IDEN OLIVER (8) will again require some luck from the inside back-row draw but cannot be ruled out with clear running at the right time. KNOCK OUT (7) has been racing well without winning and, if able to secure a nice run in transit with some genuine tempo throughout, should be finishing off strongly. Selections:SWEET DIXIE (2), EYE SEE AMOUR (5), KNOCKOUT (7), IDEN OLIVER (8)

A standing-start event over 2090 metres, where the front-line runners generally get their chance to roll along. REPETITIVE (2) continues to drop back in grade after going winless from 27 attempts this season. If he can step cleanly, he could take plenty of running down at each-way odds. OLLIES MEDAL (4) clearly possesses ability but can be his own worst enemy, and once again his chances largely depend on how well he begins. If he steps safely and behaves throughout, he should be right in the finish. SPOOKY GIRL (6) made good late ground from the back of the field in a fast mile rate last start and, if able to find a position closer to the speed in this even field, should take plenty of beating. The handicapped runners are clearly the class horses of the race, although they will require sharp beginnings to make up ground early. ZEUS IMMORTAL (8) has competed well in recent four-year-old features and makes his first standing-start appearance here, while LAID BACK (9) has been racing extremely well without winning against stronger opposition and brings a clear class edge back to this grade. Selections:SPOOKY GIRL (6), LAID BACK (9), REPETITIVE (2), ZEUS IMMORTAL (8)

A difficult race to assess, with a very even field engaged. WAZOWSKI (2) gets her chance to improve on recent form and looks capable of being the first runner to the pegs, which should give her every opportunity. Her stablemate IAMAHUNTER (1) should receive the perfect run behind the leader and gets his chance to utilise the sprint lane after competing in slightly stronger races at his past few starts. MY WAY (5) looks the other main gate-speed runner on the front row and is rarely far away in races of this grade. SHOOBEES SPIRIT (6) will be reliant on genuine tempo throughout but should be flying home late, as he usually does when saved for one run. DONNY IN PARIS (8) and CHAMONIX (9) get favourable back-row draws and, with the right luck in running, should both be finishing off strongly. Selections:IAMAHUNTER (1), MY WAY (5), SHOOBEES SPIRIT (6), WAZOWSKI (2)

A low-class event over the mile where there looks to be good speed engaged early. COLORADO GIRL (1) will no doubt be looking to hold up from the pole draw. She was well backed when narrowly defeated over the short trip two starts ago before breaking during the run last start, and gets her chance to return to the winner's circle here with better manners. FEELINKINDALUCKY (4) will again be driven positively and may look to sit outside the pole marker and out-tough her, as she did two starts back. BARBETTE (3) somewhat drops back in grade following a handy second last start and should receive a nice run with cover, giving her every opportunity to be in the finish. COLBY ART (7) and STAROFREMEMBRANCE (8) will be relying on genuine tempo throughout to bring them into the race and should be running home strongly, as they usually do. QUEENOFDANCE (9) could be the one at each-way odds from a nice trailing draw, having bobbed up a couple of times recently in this grade. Selections:COLORADO GIRL (1), FEELINKINDALUCKY (4), BARBETTE (3), QUEENOFDANCE (9)

The first of two small fields to round out the night is the higher-class event on the program, where IRON CLAD (4) and VANQUISH STRIDE (6) gain entry after not winning at their past eight starts. They hold a definite class edge over most of their opposition and would expect both to be fighting out the placings at worst. THE DEVILS FLAME (1) has been racing well since arriving in Tasmania after bringing competitive Victorian form across and gets every opportunity from the pole in the small field. He looks the most progressive runner engaged and could take plenty of holding out. MERRYWOOD PAUL (3) is racing better than his recent numerical form suggests and only needs to maintain those efforts to be highly competitive. The small field should suit after he has been making ground from the rear in recent starts. MISTA EAGLE (2) can never be ruled out in races of this nature and looks the runner most likely to pressure the pole marker early in search of the lead. ALWAYS AURORA (5) has not been on his best behaviour of late, but it would be no surprise to see him bob up and win if he puts his best foot forward. Selections:THE DEVILS FLAME (1), IRON CLAD (4), VANQUISH STRIDE (6), MERRYWOOD PAUL (3)

An absolute raffle to round out the night, where you would expect the entire field to start at single-figure odds. KENYA (5) will no doubt be driven aggressively from the outset, which is when he races at his best, and expect he may even bully his way to the front and take plenty of catching. ROSE NOIRE (2) produced an improved effort last start after joining the new stable and gets her chance to continue that progression. If she improves again, she could be very hard to hold out late. The other two old boys, DEBT TILL WE PART (4) and NO NUKES SKIPPER (6), have both bobbed up to win recently and certainly can't be ruled out in this grade. LALIBELA (3) possesses a sharp late sprint when there is genuine tempo throughout and could easily be in the finish if the race is run to suit. BRIGHTLY BLAZE (1) is a three-year-old filly taking on the older horses after returning to the state and, despite the rise in grade, it would be no surprise to see her win if she produces her best form. Selections:KENYA (5), ROSE NOIRE (2), BRIGHTLY BLAZE (1), LALIBELA (3) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:ALDEBARAN JAZMINE (5) has been freshened since a disappointing seventh at Kilmore in July. Her form prior was strong and she will take beating if she can return to her peak form. THE ITALIAN DREAM (6) finished off nicely when fourth behind BUSLIN BRODY (8) at Kilmore last week. She is trotting consistently and should be competitive again. BUSLIN BRODY (8) settled three back on the markers and finished off best via the sprint lane when he scored at Kilmore last week. He is awkwardly drawn on the inside of the second line but this is a field of similar quality so he must be considered as a winning chance again. CLASSIC FAIR (10) galloped and lost his chance when resuming but he finished a close second behind Little Miss Morgan at a Cobram trial since so he is capable of better. TWEEDLEDEE (9) settled four back on the markers and burst home late when a game second behind Vici Bloom at Melton last week. He hasn’t won in 39 starts for the season but he appears to be very well graded with a claiming price of $8,000 in this event so he cannot be discarded. SELECTIONS: ALDEBARAN JAZMINE (5), THE ITALIAN DREAM (6), BUSLIN BRODY (8), CLASSIC FAIR (10)

OVERVIEW:BET BET HOTSHOT (1) was headed off at the start and ended up being three back on the markers before finishing off well for second behind FLING IT RAINBOW (7) last week. He might end up being behind the leader here and will be dangerous via the sprint lane. PIQUE (9) made several errors and lost her chance when unplaced at Kilmore last outing. She ran a game race when second behind Keayang Minnesota at Ballarat prior and she was runner up behind the classy 2yo trotter Phoenix Red on July 24 so she is worth another chance. AGAINST THE BRIDLE (8) pushed forward to race without cover and faded into seventh at Kilmore last outing. His form prior was sound and this is a drop back in class so he is worth an investment. FLING IT RAINBOW (7) began quickly and ended up being behind the leader when he got home best to win at Kilmore last week. He has a tough draw to overcome but he won comfortably last time out. SELECTIONS: BET BET HOTSHOT (1), PIQUE (9), AGAINST THE BRIDLE (8), FLING IT RAINBOW (7)

OVERVIEW: STERLING GIGI (6) began quickly but ended up being shuffled to three back on the markers when he chased hard for second behind Kings Gallery at Melton last week. He has shown promise during his juvenile season and this appears to be a very suitable assignment. JUST MY LUCK (7) is resuming but won a trial in reasonable time at Cobram last week and is capable of showing up without surprising. ROCKINTHEKASBA (8) had every chance and dropped out from the 400m when ninth on this track at his first run since April. He performed much better in a trial prior with a runaway success so an improved showing would not surprise. DONTTELLNANNA (9) settled in a rearward position and did well over the final 200m to pick up half of the field at Cranbourne on Sunday. She is better than her form reads and rates as a value hope. ASHANTE CADMAN (5) led out then took cover when second behind Beau Beca last week. He is likely to adopt similar tactics here and is worth a ticket each way. BACK: STERLING GIGI (6) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: STERLING GIGI (6), JUST MY LUCK (7), ROCKINTHEKASBA (8), DONTTELLNANNA (9)

OVERVIEW: KINGS GALLERY (10) is a very smart juvenile pacer, which was runner up at his first four attempts and resumed with a dominant victory at Melton last week. He is taking on older horses this evening but he appears to have a very promising future. BLUE MIKI (7) circled around the field from the middle of the pack to race without cover and battled on strongly for second behind Hez Harrywho seven days ago. He is versatile and is racing consistently so he looms as one of the leading chances again. TOOBY GOLD (6) commenced from the inside of the second line and was shuffled back to seventh early before finishing off fast for an eye-catching second behind Spun Silver last week. This race is slightly tougher but she is capable of running into a place again. MIKI MARK (8) was also caught on the markers after commencing from the inside of the second line last week and didn’t have much luck. He is racing well and is worth thought in multiple combinations. BACK: KINGS GALLERY (10) – 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: KINGS GALLERY (10), BLUE MIKI (7), TOOBY GOLD (6), MIKI MARK (8)

OVERVIEW:THESTING (6) is resuming since January but he has had four recent trial performances so he should be somewhere near his peak fitness. His four race track starts to date were in the Homegrown Classic series, the Graham Head Memorial and the Holloway Classic so he appears to be well placed against this field. ARCHAA (3) is a fast beginner and has been racing in fine form at Kilmore with four wins and three placed efforts from his past seven starts. He attempted to lead throughout and ran along at a genuine tempo when third behind Shazza Love seven days ago. LIBERTY STAR DUST (8) settled in the second half of the field and produced a big finish when a game third at his first run since May. He has ability and is worth following. UNCLE TREV (5) was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off nicely for third behind Madam Reactor at Shepparton last week. That was his first up run since June and he should strip fitter so he must be included amongst the leading chances. FROSTY DROP (7) led throughout at a Cranbourne victory on June 14 and met a strong field at her latest sixth. She is poorly drawn but has the ability to figure in the finish. BACK: THESTING (6) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS: THESTING (6), ARCHAA (3), LIBERTY STAR DUST (8), UNCLE TREV (5)

OVERVIEW:PASS THE SALT (5) was resuming since a sixth in the Homegrown Classic in December when he raced without cover throughout and proved to be too strong at Kilmore last week. He should strip fitter from that performance and is a winning chance again despite rising in class. OX KNOX (6) was heavily supported and led throughout to score comfortably over Buslin Brody (won since) at Melton. He has returned from a break in good form and should prove hard to beat again. CALL ME JACK (7) will appreciate a drop back in grade from his recent efforts and he is capable of sprinting to the line quickly with the right trail forward. He is likely to settle in a rearward position early but will be suited if there is a genuine tempo throughout. STRAIGHT TO THETOP (4) is a speedy mare that finished a close second last week after leading out then taking cover. She is likely to adopt similar tactics here and has winning claims. SELECTIONS: PASS THE SALT (5), OX KNOW (6), CALL ME JACK (7), STRAIGHT TO THETOP (4)

OVERVIEW: MOISSANITE (7) is still learning and has gait issues but he has the ability to test this field. He was slow to begin and lost approximately 30m before circling around the field to race without cover when a big third behind Callinan at Ballarat. MI BOW (5) was checked at the start and lost several lengths before settling at the back of the pack then sustained a long run from the 800m when a creditable third last outing. She has been placed in five of her past six starts and deserves to break through for a win. LEZAMA (4) gained a nice trail early and was left stranded without cover from the bell when second behind Sambezia last outing. She has also been racing consistently with four placed efforts from her past five starts and warrants respect. DELTA GEE (1) is a first starter for trainer Kari Males, which finished third at a Kilmore trial effort last week and must be kept safe. BACK: MOISSANITE (7) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: MOISSANITE (7), MI BOW (5), LEZAMA (4), DELTA GEE (1)

The maiden two-year-olds kick-start the night, where CREAMY KARALTA (7) makes his debut following two impressive trial victories. He draws the outside of the front row, but looks a classy type and expect Kent Rattray to have him screwed down and ready to win first up. RYHAD (1) trialled nicely against older horses in good time recently and should take plenty of improvement from that experience, although he showed limited gate speed on that occasion. SOLO SNITCH (2) and IDEN JUST BECAUSE (8) drop back in grade after competing in recent two-year-old features and should appreciate their favourable draws, giving both every opportunity to be in the finish. POGACAR (6) and SMELL THE SMOKE (4) have both placed at the trials and look like improving types. It would be no surprise to see either take another step forward here, and they appear the best of the remainder. Selections:CREAMY KARLATA (7), SOLO SNITCH (2), IDEN JUST BECAUSE (8), RYHAD (1)

GO THE RED (2) has been a great addition to the Yole stable since arriving from Queensland and produced another handy performance in similar grade against some classy opposition last start. Expect him to be driven aggressively again here in an attempt to find the front, where he could take plenty of running down over the longer distance. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5) is a brilliant standing-start beginner and should find himself in the first couple after 200 metres. He should relish the longer journey and looks certain to be thereabouts. GORDONS BAY (6) comes from the 20-metre back mark but should get every opportunity in the small field to utilise his sharp finishing sprint. IRON CLAD (1) is rarely far away in races of this nature, as is COLBY SANZ (3), while WATERMELON SUGAR (4) could give a cheeky sight if he begins sharply, as he has done on a couple of occasions recently. Selections:GO THE RED (2), ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5), GORDONS BAY (6), IRON CLAD (1)

The maidens again go at it looking to break their duck, with several runners knocking on the door. CHARLI PIPPEN (5) continues to threaten to break through but has kept finding one better. Expect him to settle just off the speed with cover and get another opportunity to finish strongly. LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (3) will no doubt look to attempt an all-the-way victory, as he has done on several occasions recently, while LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (2) should also settle handy on the pegs and has not been far away of late. QUARTEIRA (7) is a well-bred three-year-old colt closely related to the champion Beautide and should continue to improve with further race experience. Recent mainland arrivals DIAMONDONTHEROCKS (8) and ROBUST SALLY (9) should be competitive in a maiden of this nature. DEMON DESTROYER (6) has changed stables and, although he has clearly had some gait issues throughout his short career, he was seen making nice ground in a trial earlier this week. If he brings his best manners and form to race night, he could be right in the finish. Selections:CHARLI PIPPEN, LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (3), DEMON DESTROYER (6), LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (2)

An even field where the three-year-olds A DRAGON FOR JOE (3) and OMYBACNKNEES JUDGE (2) will be looking to take advantage of their favourable front-row draws after some handy performances of late. Expect KEAYANG LEXI (1) to attempt to control the race from the front, while IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (4) should also be driven forward from the gate. That should give the three-year-olds their opportunity to secure positions on speed with cover and be right in the finish. JET TO HEAVEN (10) makes his Tasmanian debut for the visiting stable and brings handy enough mainland form to be competitive in a race of this nature. It wouldn't surprise to see any of the remaining runners bob up and earn a cheque for connections in what looks a very even affair. Selections A DRAGON FOR JOE (3), OMYBACNKNEES JUDGE (2), IFYOULOVEME LETMEGO (4), JET TO HEAVEN (10)

A competitive field with plenty of consistent performers engaged, where MUZZA MEMATE (4) is racing in career-best form. He can still be a nervous watch for punters and occasionally does something wrong, but clearly possesses the most ability in this field when at his best. Expect him to push forward from the draw, as will EVERYTHING BUT THE (2), who has been super consistent of late and may be able to find the pegs, where he could take plenty of running down and looks a danger. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (1) is always thereabouts in this grade and should again get his opportunity from a position on speed. MONEYS NO ISSUE (9) was spotted hitting the line strongly last start and should be running home well again, while MOVESLIKEALADY (12) will no doubt be doing similar from the wide back-row draw, as she usually does when saved for one run. JOHN VINCENT (10) is an interesting runner arriving from South Australia and looks to possess plenty of speed, so the market may be the best guide to his chances first up in the state. Selections:MUZZAMEMATE (4), EVERYTHING BUT THE (2), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (1)MONEYS NO ISSUE (9)

The low-class event of the night is an extremely open affair. Expect PARK LANE (4) to use his sharp gate speed in an attempt to find the front, where he could give a cheeky sight at odds over the short distance and looks a potential improver. SHEEZA SOHO (1) should enjoy a nice run in transit behind the expected speed and gets her chance to notch up another victory, being the least-experienced runner in the field. JEREMY WELLS (5) and GOBSMACKED (7) should be running home strongly, as they usually do in races of this nature. COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2) gets his opportunity to improve from a favourable draw, while HORRIE OTARA (3) and CHRIS BE QUICK (6) should again run their usual honest races. Selections:SHEEZA SOHO (1), PARK LANE (4), COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2), GOBSMACKED (7)

Trainer Charlie Castles holds the key here, with the stable appearing to have the two leading chances in the field. ATOMIC BLACK (1) possesses good gate speed and gets his chance to return to the winner's circle from the pole draw over the short trip. LOU BABY (4) should appreciate the smaller field and gets his opportunity to settle on speed and show his class after two handy performances since returning from a lengthy spell. He should now be nearing peak fitness. LYNRYD SKYNRYD (7) could be the fly in the ointment from a speed-map perspective if he is used aggressively from the gate, as he often is. ANOTHER NIEN (9) gets a nice trailing draw and is rarely far away in races of this nature. If there is genuine early speed, that should also suit SNOWIEWILLREV (2), who was an easy winner last start when coming off a hot tempo, albeit in weaker grade. He should receive another nice run in transit and be finishing off strongly. Likewise, VANQUISH STRIDE (3) can never be ruled out in this grade. Selections:ATOMIC BLACK (1), LOU BABY (4), SNOWIEWILLREV (2), VANQUISH STRIDE (3)

WEE GEORGIE WOOD (1) will be looking to take advantage of getting back to a favourable draw and gets his chance to return to the winner's circle. He can be a little touchy behind the mobile, however, so will need to bring his best manners, particularly with ART HUNTSMAN (4) likely to use his sharp gate speed in an attempt to find the pegs early. He has returned to his best form of late and continues to race very consistently. WATCH YOUR BACK (5) got the gaps at the right time when winning last start and gets his opportunity to make it back-to-back victories in this even field. IMA LITTLE NEEDY (3) should find a position on speed with cover and gets his chance after competing well in recent four-year-old features, with this representing somewhat of a drop in class. The four Wayne Yole-trained runners can never be ruled out in races of this nature, with CAN FEEL THE FURY (6) looking the pick of them after returning to his best form in recent starts. He would appreciate genuine tempo throughout to allow him to finish off strongly. Selections:WEE GEORGIE WOOD (1), ART HUNTSMAN (4), IMA LITTLE NEEDY, WATCH YOUR BACK (5)

The No More Than Three Wins Fillies and Mares event brings together a fairly even field on ability, although there is a wider spread when it comes to their handicap marks. SOHO TIGER LILY (4) should be the first runner to the pegs after competing in the Oaks last start and gets her chance to run another strong race back in this company. ALWAYSATIGER (6) drops back from the four-year-old mares features and should be finishing strongly, noting she has also undergone a stable change since her latest appearance. WEONA EAGLE (7) could be the one at odds if she can rediscover her best form, while SWEETHEART DIOR (2) has been excellent in all her starts since arriving in Tasmania, including a handy third in the Oaks last week. ALL ABOUT SADIE (1) and PHLOW JO (5) are consistent mares who rarely run poorly and will again be looking to earn a cheque for connections by finishing in the placings. OVERVIEW:JUST INCREDIBLE (6) is racing in great form and looms as the horse to beat. He worked hard in the run and went down fighting when a brave second behind the smart pacer Don Crunch at Mildura on August 07. STARVIN MARVIN (2) began quickly to lead and held off his rivals to win at Mildura two weeks ago and is a good chance of finding the lead again so he cannot be dismissed. CALF PEN (1) is racing well below his best form but this is his best draw for some time and he is a possible improver. CAULONIA TERROR (3) came from last and hit the line strongly for fourth behind Cheers Poverty last week. He has recently dropped down into this class and went well enough last week to warrant consideration. HELLAVA DEAL (4) will be fitter from her first up run since May and has the ability to show up prominently. BACK: JUST INCREDIBLE (6) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: JUST INCREDIBLE (6), STARVIN MARVIN (2), CALF PEN (1), CAULONIA TERROR (3)

OVERVIEW:SNEAKY PHILTRA (7) has had three wins and two seconds from her past six starts and sustained a long run out three horses wide from the bell when a game second behind Whitehaven Beach last week. She is a versatile mile and should take beating against this class. ACCELERE (4) was competing at Mildura back in 2023 before heading to New South Wales and Queensland. He is resuming since a second behind Artistic Saint at Redcliffe, where he settled three back on the markers and gained a one out and one back trail before the home turn. He did well when he last competed locally and he won a trial on Monday night so a bold showing would not surprise. HESASTAR (5) pushed forward to race without cover and battled on fairly for fourth at Mildura last outing. He produced a strong performance to win at Mildura prior and he should be close to the pace again here. PUNTO CALIENTE (1) settled in a rearward position, sprinted quickly down the back straight and sustained the run to win nicely last week. This is a race of more depth but he is drawn to go well again. BACK: SNEAKY PHILTRA (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: SNEAKY PHILTRA (7), ACCELERE (4), HESASTAR (5), PUNTO CALIENTE (1)

OVERVIEW: FORTY LOVE (4) was resuming since June when he went down fighting after doing all of the work in the run at his latest close third. He should strip fitter from that run and has the best draw out of the major chances so he warrants respect. DON LOU (5) made a good impression at his first run since coming from Queensland and will prove hard to beat again. He settled down midfield, came out four horses wide on the home turn and produced a big finish to defeat a field of similar standard. HOT DEAL (6) was a game winner over Ultimate Vinnie at Horsham prior to a close second behind DON LOU (5). He appeared to have his chance last outing but his record at Mildura is strong and he is tough enough to be in the finish. MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (1) will appreciate his best draw for some time and he has won several races under these conditions at Mildura previously so he is worth a ticket each way. SELECTIONS: FORTY LOVE (4), DON LOU (5), HOT DEAL (6), MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (1)

OVERVIEW: YOU’VE BEEN SERVED (7) finished strongly from three back on the markers and missed out by a narrow margin at her debut then battled on strongly after racing in the death seat at her latest Mildura performance. She is a promising filly and appears to be well placed against this class. CAPTIVATE ME (5) led out then took cover when second behind My Ultimate Henry last week. He is a good chance of finding the lead despite his wide draw and he should prove hard to catch. CRUEL MISTRESS (1) was headed off at the start and moved away from the markers to race without cover from the 1500m when third under similar conditions last week. She is ideally drawn and is not without a chance. ULTIMATE ADVICE (6) is widely drawn but should have benefited from the experience of her debut performance last week and is worth thought in multiple combinations. BACK: YOU’VE BEEN SERVED (7) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: YOU’VE BEEN SERVED (7), CAPTIVATE ME (5), CRUEL MISTRESS (1), ULTIMATE ADVICE (6)

OVERVIEW:LETSGO BIG GIRL (7) was disappointing at her latest sixth at Mildura but she performs much better over the sprint distance and this is a significant drop back in class. She recorded a sizzling mile rate of 1.56.4 when she scored at Mildura on July 10, which is a good form pointer for this event. WATCH THE ATTITUDE (5) produced a career best performance when she led throughout in a mile rate of 1.56.5 two weeks ago then followed with a second behind King Saint last week. She is a versatile mare and is worth an investment. BIGBASHASH (4) progressed forward to find the lead and won at Horsham two starts ago then endured a tough run at her latest unplaced performance. She is likely to give a forward showing from her reasonable draw. GOOD BOOTS BINDI (6) is capable of sprinting to the line quickly with the right trail forward and is racing consistently against this class so she is worth a ticket each way. SELECTIONS: LETSGO BIG GIRL (7), WATCH THE ATTITUDE (5), BIGBASHASH (4), GOOD BOOTS BINDI (6)

OVERVIEW:KEAYANG CRIPPA (4) progressed forward to race without cover and battled on fairly well for fourth behind Punto Caliente seven days ago. He is racing in good form and is a chance of finding the lead from his reasonable draw so he should prove hard to beat. EGBERT (5) is another fast beginner drawn on the front line and is working back into his peak form. He came from midfield and finished off well for a close second behind Punto Caliente last week. ALIENFROMARMSTRONG (8) was heavily supported and attempted to lead throughout when a disappointing sixth at Mildura last week. He was held up for a run at a vital stage when second prior and he came from off the speed to win at Mildura on July 10 so he is worth another chance. MAJOR LINCOLN (7) was placed in two attempts at Mildura back in 2021/22 and is returning from a long stay in the Sunshine State. He hasn’t been in the best of form of late but he does strike a suitable assignment first up for trainer Tori Hutchins. BACK: KEAYANG CRIPPA (4) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: KEAYANG CRIPPA (4), EGBERT (5), ALIENFROMARMSTRONG (8), MAJOR LINCOLN (7)

OVERVIEW: WHITEHAVEN BEACH (7) broke through for a deserved victory at Mildura last week, where he progressed forward to find the lead and kicked on too well in the run to the finish. He is awkwardly drawn but is one of the leading chances again. BAZZAS LEGACY (8) will appreciate a drop back in class for this assignment and has been placed in three of his past four starts. He enjoyed a nice trail throughout but held his own in reasonable time when second behind Cheers Poverty last week. THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (2) is a fast beginner and led throughout to win at Mildura two starts ago. He pressured the leader throughout and did extremely well for third last week so he must be considered as a winning chance again. SHES POPPY (9) is also dropping back in class for this assignment and has the speed to be in the finish. She chased hard when second in a slick mile rate of 1.56.5 at Mildura two starts ago. SELECTIONS: WHITEHAVEN BEACH (7), BAZZAS LEGACY (8), THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (2), SHES POPPY (9)

OVERVIEW: Plenty of hopes to kick-off the night of racing at Melton, but FREAK OUT (9) looks to find a suitable assignment in what is a slight drop in grade from recent outings. He was only beaten 14.7m in a slick 1:54.7 mile rate last time behind Foregone Conclusion and had similar margins in two runs before that after winning from the front in a 41-45 ratings event at Melton. This is an easier 0-41 clash and he should run well from nine. The Glenn Bull runners FAVOURITEHIGHLIGHT (8), who draws for a good trip behind speedy beginner OHHEMMJAY CRESCO (1), and SHEZABLUECHIP (3), who has been brave despite tough trips her past couple, look good chances, while GOODTIME MAE (6) is among a host of others that wouldn’t surprise with the right trip. Tough start! SELECTIONS: FREAK OUT (9), FAVOURITEHIGHLIGHT (8), SHEZABLUECHIP (3), GOODTIME MAE (6)

OVERVIEW: Another race where you can make a case for quite a few, but siding with KYVALLEY MICHAEL (9) from the back row. He looks to be the horse contesting the best races of late, and he has been very competitive in doing so. He had no real chance last weekend when settling at the tail in a race won by leader Vici Bloom, but before that sat parked and only went down 4.6m to Sky Flair, who has won again since. That was in a 0-75 ratings race, and this is a drop back to a 56-64 event. The in-form DISTANT SUN (7) is a good chance despite the wide gate. He was a big winner two starts back for Blake Pace when unleashing a great turn of foot to run down Ox Knox at Kilmore, and was very brave when second to SEBASTIANS WAITING (8) at the same track when bringing up the running line from near the tail on August 6. The latter ruined his chances of back-to-back wins when galloping early last start but was only beaten 11.2m and is a handy type, while SCAR (4) might be a chance to get down to the fence and perhaps heads the rest of the winning chances. BACK: KYVALLEY MICHAEL (9) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY MICHAEL (9), DISTANT SUN (7), SEBASTIANS WAITING (8), SCAR (4)

OVERVIEW: Such a hard race to map over the 1200m, but PISTOL PEARCE (5) might have the early toe to cross at the start and from there would take a lot of beating across a distance where the fence is gold. He’s certainly no superstar, but he did lead and win here at Melton last time out and also at Geelong in a slick last half on June 19. BULLETPROOF KID (2) has been runner-up his past three and looks a logical danger, while HITCH TO HIS STAR (9) and HITTHEROADJACK (8) are probably the class factors but have awkward draws to navigate. Both have good form around nice horses at Melton on a Saturday night and can certainly win if the tempo is frantic up top, as can HIGHLANDHARTBREAKA (7). SELECTIONS: PISTOL PEARCE (5), BULLETPROOF KID (2), HITCH TO HIS STAR (9), HITTHEROADJACK (8)

OVERVIEW: MISS MUSCLE (5) is a two-year-old trotter up against mostly older horses, but looks fairly smart and might be able to add a second career win to her resume. She won in good style at Melton two starts back and then chased home the very handy Phoenix Rex for third after that, getting close to Regal Gala who has won since. THE CHOOK (1) draws for a nice trip, and while disappointing as favourite last time out at Kilmore, has run some good races prior and looks a threat. SHES SKY HIGH (8) should lob a nice spot on the fence and is dropping back in grade a shade, while DREAMS OF LOVE (2) looks a chance of crossing down to the fence where she would run a good race second-up from a break. HOLD THAT MAGIC (9) has trialled okay since her last run and is one to factor in for wider exotics, and while two-year-old MAJARO GIRL (3) might start well in the market, I haven’t been overly taken by her two runs for the Andy Gath yard. BACK: MISS MUSCLE (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MISS MUSCLE (5), THE CHOOK (1), SHES SKY HIGH (8), DREAMS OF LOVE (2)

OVERVIEW: Looks plenty of speed off the front line here and it won’t be easy for THE FINAL DANCE (1), but he has started odds-on in all four runs since joining the Emma Stewart stable and won two of them in good style. The defeats had excuses, including last time over 1200m when he was crossed at the start and had to do work. He still closed well and was only beaten 5.4m by the handy Insider Trading. He’s no moral, but from the draw he goes on top. FIRE MARSHALL (10) hasn’t been seen at the trials since his last run on June 13, which was a brave death-seat fourth to the seasoned Clymenus. This followed a number of nice efforts on Saturday nights at Melton and he’s certainly a contender first-up from a freshen. TIVOLI (8) should get a nice run in behind THE FINAL DANCE (1) and is very capable in this grade, while MONTANA PRIDE (9) chased down ISTHISTHEREALLIFE (7) on August 3 and then wasn’t beaten far last time out behind Pistol Pearce. Those two are also contenders in a race where you can make a case for plenty of runners. SELECTIONS: THE FINAL DANCE (1), FIRE MARSHALL (10), TIVOLI (8), MONTANA PRIDE (9)

OVERVIEW: LENARD ESS (1) is a veteran of 195 career starts and loves the peg-line runs, which he will get here. He hasn’t done much his last couple when off the fence, but did run a nice second to the handy The Last Trip at Geelong recently and should give this a real shake from barrier one if he can do enough to boot up and perhaps take a sit on fast beginner SPUN SILVER (5). MISS PIGGY WIGGY (9) closed off okay from the rear in the race won by SPUN SILVER (5) at Melton last week and can improve on that with a different race shape over the 2240m, WOODLEA DIEGO (2) is another of the quick starters off the front line and is a winning factor, while the grey SPUN SILVER (5) is probably better suited over the shorter trips, but is flying at the moment and will give herself a chance if she can again find her favourite spot out in front. SELECTIONS: LENARD ESS (1), MISS PIGGY WIGGY (9), WOODLEA DIEGO (2), SPUN SILVER (5)

OVERVIEW: LITTLE MISS MORGAN (2) has trialled really nicely at Cobram since her fourth placing here at Melton on August 7 when she made an early break but still did a great job to only be beaten 14.5m. She was only nabbed in the shadows of the post by the in-form Spirited Lass prior to that and her first-up win during July was very good. While her manners are always a concern, a faultless display will have her hard to beat, particularly if she finds the front. Great to see the return of last season’s Victorian 2YO Trotting Filly of the Year HARPERSEVEN (6), who heads into her first run as a three-year-old on the back of three trials. She won the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series final last season and must be respected in this grade. MET WITH A SHRUG (1) is going great guns for Team Murphy and chased well for second behind the smart The Preacher last time, while KEAYANG MINNESOTA (8) is two from two this campaign and is the other key winning hope alongside the unbeaten LORD LOGAN (3), who has been so impressive despite death seat trips in two wins to start his career. BACK: LITTLE MISS MORGAN (2) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: LITTLE MISS MORGAN (2), HARPERSEVEN (6), MET WITH A SHRUG (1), KEAYANG MINNESOTA (8)

OVERVIEW: FANTASY FLIGHT (8) was $1.10 favourite last time at Kilmore when he galloped early and ruined his chances at the start. Nothing went right there and we should go off his prior first-up run when he found the front, gave a great kick and was only nailed late by Bay Of Fires in good time. There was a huge margin back to third and he looks ready to break his maiden at the eighth time of asking. SWEETSUGARCANDYMAN (1) was super at the trials last time out when coming from a mile back to win at Melton and looks a good chance on debut, SWEET FLORABEL (5) beat the aforementioned rival home when second at her only trial appearance on August 4 and is another that steps out on debut, while BETTER THEN DAICOS (3) showed gate speed to lead last time at Shepparton, and despite dropping out there was well fancied in the market and is best of the rest alongside ARRIVAL TIME (6). BACK: FANTASY FLIGHT (8) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: FANTASY FLIGHT (8), SWEETSUGARCANDYMAN (1), BETTER THEN DAICOS (3), SWEET FLORABEL (5)

OVERVIEW: DONNYOSKO (4) is the most experienced horse in this field of two-year-old trotters and she’s shown enough ability in her five starts to suggest she’s capable of winning a maiden this season. She broke when in a striking position during a recent trial at Maryborough, but her first-up run when fourth at the same track on August 3 was serviceable and her efforts before a spell earlier in the year were sound. SNOWIN (3) chased home race winner Rose All Day to only be beaten 4m in a trial at Kilmore and steps out on debut for the powerhouse Andy Gath yard, no vision was available for KYVALLEY DRIFTER’s (1) trial at Melton on August 11 but she won that and also hails from a strong trotting stable, while LUSTROUS (5) has been okay in a couple of trial hit-outs ahead of his debut. A race where we will learn a bit!
